request.title: Neon Salvage
request.prompt: Implement the next studio task from phone gameplay review #34 in the existing Neon Salvage game: make each earned pickup reward readable while dragging. Show a short, legible label such as '+10 · x1' or '+20 · x2' above the collected core, offset from the touch point and clamped inside the arena. Use the points and multiplier actually awarded BEFORE the existing multiplier advances; the NEXT CORE HUD continues to show the next reward multiplier. Keep the number and lifetime of labels bounded. Labels must not intercept touch, obscure the ship, or cover the HUD. Respect reduced motion with a stationary alternative. Pause freezes feedback lifetimes, and restart/replay clears them. Preserve the scoring rules, x5 cap, damage/reset behavior, hull, one-minute end conditions, controls, layout and existing game URL. Extend the existing read-only snapshot with a copied pickupFeedback array (points, multiplier, x, y, ttl) from actual live feedback state so the feature can be checked without state mutation. Read review #34 as evidence; the recording's time discontinuity is not a confirmed timer defect. Run the existing Neon Salvage logic harness and document your actual feature checks. Deliver a tested update of this game.
acceptance: The first two pickups visibly report +10 at x1 and +20 at x2 using the awarded multiplier; capped pickups report +50 at x5. Existing NEXT CORE progression and scoring stay correct.
Reward labels are legible above the pickup/touch location, stay inside the playable area, and do not intercept touch input or obscure the ship or HUD.
Feedback is bounded in count and lifetime, freezes while paused, expires during play, and clears on restart/replay. Reduced-motion mode keeps the reward readable without floating animation.
The read-only diagnostic snapshot exposes fresh copies of actual pickupFeedback state for verification; it cannot mutate gameplay.
Run node --check for game.js, node game_factory/check_neon_logic.cjs, and concrete pickup-feedback checks; retain functional mobile start/drag/pause/resume/restart and the 60-second result flow.

producer.claim: Implement a pickup reward feedback system in Neon Salvage that visually displays the exact points and multiplier earned upon collecting a core while dragging, without disrupting existing gameplay mechanics or UI elements.
producer.rationale: The request specifies a concise, legible floating label such as '+10 · x1' or '+20 · x2' above the collected core, offset from the touch point, clamped inside the arena, and showing the awarded points and current multiplier before advancement. Labels should be bounded in number and lifetime, not intercept touch, obscure the ship or HUD, respect reduced motion mode with a stationary alternative, and freeze lifetimes during pause. The existing NEXT CORE HUD should continue displaying the next multiplier. Restart/replay clears all feedback labels. Extend the existing readonly snapshot with a copied pickupFeedback array for verification. Scoring rules, multiplier cap, damage/reset behavior, controls, HUD layout, and the one-minute session must remain unchanged. The update must be tested with automated logic checks and real gameplay simulation as per existing studio workflows.
producer.objections: Uncertainty exists whether the label positioning near the finger can always stay inside the arena and not overlap disallowed UI or gameplay elements on small screen sizes or during fast dragging. Potential performance impact from managing multiple feedback labels especially on low-end devices is not clearly addressed. The precise visual style, font size, color, and animation details must be carefully balanced for legibility and accessibility, including reduced motion mode compliance. Existing live snapshot extension must be implemented carefully to avoid unintended mutation of gameplay state. No prior code or independent QA evidence of pickup feedback implementation is present in the source, so this is untested new functionality. Physical device testing and independent QA validation remain necessary to confirm robustness and user experience.
producer.proposed_action: Scope and implement a pickup feedback label system that meets all described criteria: floating reward labels appear and fade above the pickup location offset from the touch point; they show awarded points and multiplier before increment; they cap count and lifetime; they pause when game is paused and clear on restart/replay; they respect reduced motion preference showing stationary labels; they never intercept input or obscure key elements; and they extend the snapshot with a copied pickupFeedback array reflecting current feedbacks. Verify by automated logic tests, manual gameplay runs, and snapshot inspections. No other gameplay or UI changes beyond this functionality. Measure completion by passing the provided acceptance criteria and correctness checks, including visible labels for the first few pickups matching awarded points, bounded label count, freeze on pause, clearing on restart, and snapshot exposure without mutations.
required_evidence: Automated test results from running node game_factory/check_neon_logic.cjs confirming no breakage of existing game logic and correct pickup feedback behavior.
Manual gameplay verification recording or logs demonstrating visible pickup feedback labels corresponding exactly to the awarded points and multiplier before increment.
Screenshots or video demonstrating labels positioned inside arena, offset from touch point, not intercepting input, obscuring ship or HUD.
Demonstration of labels pausing when the game is paused and clearing promptly on restart/replay.
Snapshot JSON output from window.BORHEZ_GAME.snapshot showing a copied, read-only pickupFeedback array accurately reflecting active feedback labels during play.
Confirmation that reduced motion preference disables animation and uses stationary labels, verified by toggling system setting or equivalent simulation.

researcher.claim: The current Neon Salvage game implements core gameplay and scoring with a salvage-chain multiplier, showing NEXT CORE HUD updates, and supports pause, restart, keyboard and touch controls, one-minute sessions, and hull management.
researcher.rationale: The supplied source code and prior update reveal a game where the player drags a salvage ship in a 360x480 arena, collecting cyan cores for 10 points times the current multiplier, which increases by 1 per pickup capped at x5. Colliding with red debris reduces hull by 1 and resets multiplier to x1 with a visible 'CHAIN LOST · RESET TO x1' HUD message. Time counts down from 60 seconds; when zero or hull reaches 0 the game ends with a message and replay option. Controls include pointer drag and WASD/arrows. HUD elements show score, time, multiplier, hull, and chain loss feedback. The game state snapshot includes non-mutating copies of position, score, time, hull, multiplier and arrays of cores and debris. Pause freezes time and simulation, while restart resets game state. The prior QA evidence includes multiple automated and headless browser tests confirming these behaviors, and physical device video showing correct HUD updates and damage reset feedback. The code uses no external assets or dependencies, drawing all elements with Canvas 2D. Reduced motion preference disables animations on cores and sparks, maintaining accessibility. The next update task is to add legible pickup feedback labels near touch points reflecting awarded points before multiplier increment, while preserving all existing mechanics and respecting layout constraints.
objections: No current implementation of pickup reward feedback labels is present; this is untested new functionality introducing UI elements near touch points, which may cause overlapping or occlusion issues or performance impact on low-end devices.
Positioning labels inside the arena while offset from touch and avoiding ship, HUD, or intercepting input is complex and not yet demonstrated.
The snapshot extension of pickup feedback states must be carefully done to avoid mutating live game state, yet this has no existing sample code or test results.
The reduced motion mode compliance for the new labels requires verification with system preference toggling or simulation.
Physical device and independent QA testing evidence for the pickup feedback feature is missing and still required for production readiness.

Limit the number of simultaneous labels and their lifetime, pausing lifetime decrements while the game is paused and clearing labels on restart/replay. Respect reduced motion by omitting floating animation and using stationary labels. Ensure labels have pointer-events disabled to not intercept touch input. Extend the game state snapshot to include a copied, read-only pickupFeedback array with points, multiplier, x, y, and ttl for external verification. Preserve all existing game mechanics, scoring rules, controls, HUD layout, and one-minute session behavior. Perform automated logic tests, run manual gameplay tests (including pause, restart), inspect snapshots, and validate reduced motion compliance. designer.claim: Neon Salvage’s core loop is a 60-second one-finger drag control to move a salvage ship around a 360x480 arena, collecting cyan cores for increasing score with a salvage-chain multiplier, while avoiding moving red debris that damages hull; the game provides clear visual feedback on pickups, damage, multiplier, and end conditions, supporting pause, restart, and respecting system reduced motion.
designer.rationale: The game runs continuously when started, updating player position towards a single touch point or keyboard input at a consistent speed, clamped inside arena bounds. Collecting a core awards 10 points times the current multiplier, which increments by 1 capped at x5; pickup feedback labels show awarded points and multiplier before increment, positioned near the touch but clamped inside the arena without obstructing ship, HUD, or intercepting input. Damage resets multiplier, reduces hull by one, shows chaining loss feedback, and activates invincibility frames. Visual feedback includes flashing hit effects, spark bursts on pickup and damage, HUD updates for score, time, multiplier, hull, and chain loss messages. Pausing freezes game time and feedback lifetimes; restarting resets all game state and clears feedback. Reduced motion mode disables floating animations for cores, sparks, and pickup labels for accessibility. Keyboard and touch controls coexist. The game exposes a read-only snapshot of state including a copied pickupFeedback array for external verification. The implementation preserves all original mechanics, UI layout, and scoring rules as per the studio contract.
objections: Exact positioning of pickup feedback labels near touch points could sometimes risk overlapping with ship or HUD elements on small or unusual screen sizes; careful clamping may not resolve all edge cases.
Management of multiple simultaneous labels may impact performance on low-end devices, though the count and lifetime are bounded.

Visual style, font size, and colors of pickup feedback must be well balanced for readability and accessibility, especially in reduced motion mode, but this depends on user environment and device capabilities.
The snapshot extension to include pickupFeedback is a new addition and needs thorough testing to ensure no unintended mutation of live game state occurs.
Physical device testing of the new pickup label feature and their interaction with touch input is missing, leaving some uncertainty about real-world mobile performance.
No independent QA or user feedback is yet available to confirm the usability and playability impact of the pickup feedback labels.
designer.proposed_action: Implement the pickup feedback system as floating text labels appearing above collected cores, offset from the pointer by a fixed vertical and horizontal margin, clamped inside the arena boundaries to avoid input interception and visual obstruction. Limit the maximum number of concurrent labels and set a fixed lifetime after which they fade out. Freeze label lifetimes when the game is paused, and clear them immediately on restart or replay. Respect system reduced motion settings by disabling floating animations for labels and showing them stationary. Implement pointer-events: none on labels to prevent touch interference. Extend the readonly game snapshot with a copied, read-only pickupFeedback array (each containing points, multiplier, x, y, ttl) for verification by the framework and QA tools. critic.claim: The current plan to implement pickup reward feedback labels in Neon Salvage risks multiple concrete failure cases in real mobile scenarios due to untested assumptions in label responsiveness, positioning, input handling, and state management.
critic.rationale: The plan adds floating, legible point labels above collected cores offset from the touch point, bounded in count/lifetime, with pause-aware lifetime control and snapshot exposure. It respects reduced motion and clamping inside arena boundaries, while disabling pointer events to prevent input interception. However, the absence of physical device testing leaves uncertainty if start events reliably initiate the run on varied touch hardware or if fake progress scenarios (labels appearing irrelevant to actual pickups) may occur. Touch input can easily lag or shift, risking labels overlapping HUD, ship, or going out of viewport on small or altered screen sizes or under rapid drag gestures. The code must handle pause/presume and restart cleanly to freeze and clear labels exactly without leaving stale visual artifacts. The snapshot extension requires careful cloning to avoid live game state mutation. The overall design assumes that labels never intercept input due to CSS pointer-events:none, but mobile browser event propagation and hit testing can be inconsistent. Given the complexity of input states (pointer capture, multiple pointer events), labels near touch points might still interfere with UI. Balance of label count and lifetime impacts performance on low-end devices but is not quantitatively addressed. Reduced motion compliance depends on system setting detection and animation logic correctness, which requires toggled testing. The plan has no evidence of handling or testing failure cases such as unresponsive game start, fake/delayed feedback labels, label overflow beyond viewport, or interaction with pause/restart race conditions.
objections: Unresponsive start is plausible if touchstart is blocked or ignored on some devices or if pointer capture fails, preventing expected label creation tied to pickups.
Fake progress: feedback labels may show outdated or buffered points if pickups triggered but multiplier state is incomplete or corrupted, causing misleading player feedback.
Touch input: rapid or multi-touch drag can cause label positioning conflict or overlapping with HUD or ship, violating the requirement that labels do not obscure UI or intercept touch.
Pause and restart actions require robust clearing and freezing of feedback labels; improper handling may leave persistent or desynchronized labels during or after pause.

Viewport overflow: clamping label positions inside arena must consider realistic UI margins and varying device screen aspect ratios; otherwise labels may be partially clipped or obscure controlled elements on small phones.
Balance: the maximum number and lifetime of labels is not concretely limited or tested under rapid pickups, risking visual clutter or performance degradation on low-end hardware.

Missing prompt requirements include explicit testing results for physical mobile devices, independent QA validation of UI and input handling, and verified snapshot immutability for pickupFeedback arrays.
critic.proposed_action: Implement monitoring and fail-safe mechanisms for pointer event handling and game start triggers to ensure reliable responsiveness. Add defensive logic to synchronize label feedback tightly with actual awarded points and multiplier states, avoiding fake or stale labels. Enhance label positioning algorithms to respect dynamic viewport dimensions, UI overlays, and safe input zones, verified by real device testing covering multiple screen sizes and orientations. Introduce clear lifecycle management to freeze label timers on pause, clear all labels immediately on restart, and prevent feedback persistence or desynchronization. Quantitatively set and test upper bounds for maximum simultaneous labels and their lifetimes to prevent clutter and performance issues. Extend test coverage explicitly to include physical device manual playtests and independent QA confirming the absence of input interference, accessibility compliance especially reduced motion adherence, and snapshot state safety. Provide visual evidence of labels not intercepting input or obscuring ship/HUD by observing touch or pointer hit tests on real devices. Only after such comprehensive validation should this feature proceed to production.

coder_report:
# Neon Salvage update 003

Implemented in `docs/games/neon-salvage/game.js`; existing URL, HTML, CSS, controls, layout, scoring, hull/damage rules and timer remain unchanged. Read job.json, plan.json and feedback.md (review #34). The recording discontinuity was not treated as a timer defect.

## Implementation

- Each actual core collision captures its awarded multiplier and points before incrementing NEXT CORE. Labels render `+10 · x1`, `+20 · x2`, through `+50 · x5`.
- Canvas draws bold 16px light text on a dark, cyan-bordered 104×28 panel. No new DOM/input layer is introduced, so labels cannot intercept pointer events.
- Initial placement is above the pickup with a horizontal offset, clamped inside the arena. Safe-slot positioning avoids the ship/protection ring, current drag target, other labels, and the upper area used by damage and chain-loss notices. At upper edges a side position provides clearance when above is unavailable. Positions in diagnostics match rendered panel centers.
- At most four labels live for 1.2 simulation seconds. Normal feedback rises slowly and fades near expiry. Reduced motion disables both rise and fade; safety relocation remains possible if the player later steers through a label.
- Feedback updates only during running simulation, freezes while paused, expires during play, and clears in setup for restart/replay.
- `snapshot().pickupFeedback` returns a new array of new plain objects containing points, multiplier, x, y and ttl from live feedback state. Mutating returned data does not affect gameplay.

## Commands and actual results

- `node --check docs/games/neon-salvage/game.js`: PASS.
- `node game_factory/check_neon_logic.cjs`: PASS, repeated after final changes. Existing harness verified actual collection/scoring, chain growth/reset, damage/protection, loss/replay, pause/restart, snapshot isolation, and surviving to exactly 60 seconds.
- `node <<'JS' ... JS` focused VM checks: PASS in both reduced-motion settings. Used the existing harness's seeded environment and real pointer-driven collection against unmodified game source; no gameplay-state injection or diagnostic mutation used to manufacture progress. Checked first and second awards and NEXT CORE values; naturally collected through the x5 cap; observed four simultaneous labels; checked positive TTL ≤1.2, panel bounds, ship clearance, paused state equality, resumed expiry, clean restart and copied-snapshot isolation. Reduced motion held x/y stationary across a running tick; normal mode moved y upward while TTL decreased.
- Representative snapshots: first `{points:10,multiplier:1,x:132.7355757150799,y:185.74448910262436,ttl:1.2}` with NEXT CORE x2; second reduced-motion sample `{points:20,multiplier:2,x:268,y:104,ttl:1.1999999999999997}` with NEXT CORE x3. Capped pickup reported points 50, multiplier 5.
- Additional inline Node VM Canvas command capture: PASS; actual draw calls included `+10 · x1` and `+20 · x2` at live feedback coordinates.
- An initial combined exploratory check appended extra pickup runs before the original survival fixture. Feedback assertions passed, but the altered random sequence caused that pilot to lose hull at 27.225 seconds. Separated feature checks from the unchanged deterministic survival harness; both final checks passed. No timer or difficulty changes made.
- `git diff --check`: PASS.
- `python3 -m http.server 8765 --directory docs`: blocked by sandbox socket creation (`PermissionError: Operation not permitted`).
- `node game_factory/mobile_acceptance.cjs`: attempted; blocked before gameplay by Chrome startup failure (`setsockopt: Operation not permitted`, SIGTRAP). A separate local-file Playwright attempt was blocked by a missing default headless browser executable. No dependencies installed and no tests changed.

## Limitations

Browser screenshots, real browser touch hit-testing and visual legibility on hardware could not be verified in this environment. Canvas draw commands and VM simulation are feature evidence, not physical-phone or independent QA approval. The runner must perform independent browser acceptance in its supplied environment. No deployment performed.
